items.title: 67802_Charles Mingus oral history interview
items.q: So I guess [one of] Freddy Webster (inaudible) on my influence, but I admired his playing and style of playing

ctx.x: That's the reason why the music I was playing was so different from Charlie Parker. Everybody else was playing bebop. Because I still thought there was something more important than just playing or writing tunes on the blues or some other tune with a different melody. Although Bird did play some hard (inaudible) compositions, I felt it was better if he wrote his own compositions, chord structure and all. Which most of the time he didn't. If he did do that, he did it to a blues structure. Which (inaudible) nobody,…

I liked Bird, but I don't think he influenced me that much. I was influenced by Ellington. Freddy Webster, I liked Freddy Webster's Pass the Barrel, although some people say that Pass the Barrel came from Bird. But according to Fats, Freddy Webster was already playing those type of lines that Bird was playing, before Bird was even heard of. (Singing.)
Which is not bebop, but that was the kind of lines I liked. Freddy playing with Jimmy Nelson's band. His sound was so big. He used to play the ballad Stardust. Little kids in the audience
